questions.question: When can you cross a solid yellow line?

options.text: To pass other traffic going the same direction.
Only during daylight hours.
Anytime.
When turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: When turning.
questions.explanation: You can cross broken lines, but not solid lines. You may only cross a solid yellow line when you are turning.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing with no warning lights or gates?

options.text: Cross quickly as soon as possible.
Always stop before crossing.
Be ready to yield to any train.
Speed up to cross before a train arrives.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to any train.
questions.explanation: Always be prepared to yield to trains at railroad crossings, especially when there are no lights or gates. Only cross when your entire vehicle can fit on the other side. Do not shift gears while crossing the tracks.

questions.question: What is the first thing you should do when visibility gets worse?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Slow down.
Turn on your windshield wipers.
Look for road edge markings to guide you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slowing down should be your first response when visibility decreases and road conditions become dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A narrow bridge is ahead.
A lane ends or the road narrows ahead.
An industrial area.
A freeway on-ramp is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lane ends or the road narrows ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on yellow. They tell drivers about hazards ahead. This sign warns that the right lane is ending or the road is getting narrower.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow arrow traffic signal?

options.text: Move into the lane that the arrow points to.
Slow down and stop if it is safe to do so.
Turn left after letting oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass.
Go ahead — you have the right-of-way and oncoming traffic will stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow will come next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, what should you do?

options.text: Always have the right-of-way over vehicles in a crosswalk.
Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are coming.
Enter a crosswalk anytime because drivers must stop.
Use crosswalks only when they are convenient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are coming.
questions.explanation: Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a vehicle close by may not be able to stop in time.

questions.question: You are backing out of your driveway and see children playing nearby. What should you do first?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children.
Honk your horn so the children hear you.
Walk to the back of the car to check that the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of the car to check that the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, look through your back window for people and obstacles. Do not rely only on mirrors, especially around children. Get out and check behind your vehicle before backing into or out of a driveway.

questions.question: What is the best way to merge onto a freeway?

options.text: Go slowly and wait for an opening.
Speed up faster than the traffic on the freeway.
Turn on your hazard lights until you are safely on the freeway.
Speed up to match the speed of freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Use the on-ramp to speed up to match freeway traffic so you blend in smoothly and safely. You must yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: In winter, how do overpasses and bridges compare to other roads?

options.text: They freeze and thaw at the same rate as other roads.
They freeze after other roads do.
They thaw before other roads do.
They freeze before other roads do.

questions.correctAnswerText: They freeze before other roads do.
questions.explanation: In winter, be extra careful on bridges and overpasses. They freeze before other roads and stay icy longer. Even when ice and snow look solid, they are still slippery.

questions.question: If a vehicle's high beams are pointed at you, where should you look?

options.text: Either side of the road.
The center of the road.
The right side of the road.
The left side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If an oncoming vehicle has high beams on and will not dim them, look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and lets you see enough to stay on your path until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: Your vehicle's accelerator sticks open while you are driving on a busy street. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Press hard on the brakes.
Turn on your four-way flashers.
Turn off the ignition carefully. Do not turn it far enough to lock the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the ignition carefully. Do not turn it far enough to lock the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If the accelerator sticks, the vehicle will keep going even if you lift your foot off the gas. Turn off the ignition slowly. Only turn it enough to stop the engine—not so far that it locks the steering wheel. Then use the brakes and move the vehicle safely off the road.

questions.question: What is the best way to stay safe when backing up your vehicle?

options.text: Honk your horn right before you put the car in reverse.
Check behind the vehicle before you sit in the driver's seat.
Look in your rearview mirrors to see what is behind you.
Turn up the radio before backing up to alert people around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind the vehicle before you sit in the driver's seat.
questions.explanation: Backing up is dangerous because you cannot see well behind your vehicle. Walk to the back of the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat. Look for children and small objects that might be behind it.

questions.question: What are regulatory signs?

options.text: Signs placed wherever there is an immediate danger.
Signs that tell you what you must or must not do.
Signs that are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
Signs that warn you about school zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signs that tell you what you must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular with white background and black words. They tell drivers what they must or must not do. They show speed limits, tell you not to pass or turn, and explain other driving rules.

questions.question: You are turning left onto a one-way street. Which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The right lane.
The lane closest to the lane you came from.
Either lane.
Neither lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the lane you came from.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane that is closest to where you came from. This keeps your turn safe and smooth.

questions.question: What does a speed restriction sign show?

options.text: It can be ignored when it rains, snows, or is icy.
It is triangle-shaped.
It is blue with black letters.
It shows a recommended speed for a curve or turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: It shows a recommended speed for a curve or turn.
questions.explanation: Curve and turn warning signs often have a smaller speed sign below them. This speed sign shows the safe speed for that curve or turn. You should follow this speed even if you feel you could go faster. Always slow down more when it rains, snows, or is icy.

questions.question: What do fluorescent yellow-green signs indicate?

options.text: School zones.
Hospitals.
Speed limits.
Railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zones.
questions.explanation: Fluorescent yellow-green is used for signs about schools, pedestrians, and bicycles. Drive extra carefully when you see these signs.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is coming.
Look both ways before crossing the intersection.
Always come to a full stop at this intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if you need to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if you need to.
questions.explanation: When you see a yield sign, slow down as you approach the intersection. Be ready to stop and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. You must stop completely if traffic requires it.

questions.question: Why is it important to watch for motorcycles?

options.text: They are harder to see than cars.
They rarely use their headlights.
Motorcyclists are less skilled than other drivers.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and easy to miss. They can hide in your blind spot. It is hard to judge how fast they are going or how far away they are. Always watch carefully for motorcycles.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spot when changing lanes to the left?

options.text: Glance over your right shoulder.
Look at your side mirror.
Glance over your left shoulder.
Look at your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Glance over your left shoulder.
questions.explanation: To check your blind spot, look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow mean in a traffic signal?

options.text: It is never used in traffic signals.
It means the same thing as a circular red traffic light.
Drivers may turn in the direction the arrow points.
Traffic must move in the direction the arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a circular red traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow has the same meaning as a red traffic light. When you see a red arrow, you must stop. You cannot turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light means the same thing as a:

options.text: Solid red light.
Stop sign.
Yield sign.
Caution sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop, just like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop. Then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A train station is ahead.
Signal before you go.
Slow down and let trains pass.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let trains pass.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a railroad crossing ahead. Slow down when you approach it. Trains cannot move out of your way, so you must wait for them to pass before you cross the tracks.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Sharp turn toward the curb.
Slight turn to the right.
Sharp turn away from the curb.
Keep wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sharp turn away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply away from the curb when parking uphill. This stops your car from rolling into traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: What does a solid white line in the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Do not pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. You may pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Do not pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction. You may pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction. Do not pass.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: At a stop sign, after stopping, you should:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for cars behind you.
Go when the car in front of you goes.
Look right, then left, then right again.
Look left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left first because vehicles from the left are closer to you. Then look right. Then look left again to make sure you did not miss anything.
